templates.pattern: Light travels from air into a medium at a speed of [V] × 10⁶ m/s. Calculate the refractive index of the medium. (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
templates.explanation:
Refractive index n = c ÷ v
= 3 × 10⁸ ÷ ([V] × 10⁶)
= 300 ÷ [V]
= [RESULT]

A refractive index of 1 means the speed equals the speed of light in a vacuum. Most glass has a refractive index between 1.5 and 1.9.

templates.pattern: A ray of light travels from air into glass of refractive index [N]. The angle of incidence is [AI] degrees. Calculate the sine of the angle of refraction.
templates.explanation:
Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
With n₁ = 1 (air) and n₂ = [N]:
sin θ₂ = sin [AI]° ÷ [N]
= [SINI] ÷ [N]
= [RESULT]

Snell's law applies at every boundary where light changes medium. The refracted ray bends toward the normal when entering a denser medium.

templates.pattern: A glass block has a refractive index of [N]. Calculate the sine of the critical angle for total internal reflection.
templates.explanation:
sin C = 1 ÷ n
= 1 ÷ [N]
= [RESULT]

The critical angle is the minimum angle of incidence inside the denser medium at which total internal reflection occurs. Beyond this angle no light escapes into the less dense medium.

templates.pattern: A converging lens of focal length [F] cm produces an image at a distance of [V] cm from the lens. Calculate the magnification produced by the lens.
templates.explanation:
Object distance u = vF ÷ (v − F)
= [V] × [F] ÷ ([V] − [F]) = [U] cm

Magnification = v ÷ u
= [V] ÷ [U]
= [RESULT]

The magnification tells us how many times larger the image is compared to the object.

templates.pattern: A converging lens of focal length [F] cm produces an image [V] cm from the lens. Calculate the object distance in cm.
templates.explanation:
Lens formula rearranged:
u = vF ÷ (v − F)
= [V] × [F] ÷ ([V] − [F])
= [V*F] ÷ [V-F]
= [RESULT] cm

This tells us how far the object must be placed from the lens to produce an image at distance v.

templates.pattern: A converging lens has a focal length of [F] cm. Calculate the power of the lens in dioptres.
templates.explanation:
Power = 1 ÷ focal length (in metres)
= 100 ÷ focal length (in cm)
= 100 ÷ [F]
= [RESULT] dioptres

Power is measured in dioptres (D). A converging lens has positive power. A diverging lens has negative power. Opticians use this unit for spectacle prescriptions.

templates.pattern: A lens has a power of [P] dioptres. Calculate the focal length of the lens in cm.
templates.explanation:
Focal length = 1 ÷ power (in metres)
= 100 ÷ power (in cm)
= 100 ÷ [P]
= [RESULT] cm

The higher the power of a lens the shorter its focal length and the more strongly it converges or diverges light.

templates.pattern: Two thin lenses of powers [P1] dioptres and [P2] dioptres are placed in contact. Calculate the combined power of the lens system in dioptres.
templates.explanation:
Combined power = P₁ + P₂
= [P1] + [P2]
= [RESULT] dioptres

When lenses are placed in contact their powers simply add together. This makes it easy to design lens systems for spectacles and cameras.

templates.pattern: Two thin lenses of focal lengths [F1] cm and [F2] cm are placed in contact. Calculate the combined focal length of the lens system in cm.
templates.explanation:
Combined focal length:
1/F = 1/F₁ + 1/F₂
F = F₁ × F₂ ÷ (F₁ + F₂)
= [F1] × [F2] ÷ ([F1] + [F2])
= [F1*F2] ÷ [F1+F2]
= [RESULT] cm

The combined focal length is always shorter than the shorter individual focal length.

templates.pattern: An object lies at a real depth of [R] cm beneath the surface of a liquid of refractive index [N]. Calculate the apparent depth of the object when viewed from directly above in cm.
templates.explanation:
Apparent depth = real depth ÷ refractive index
= [R] ÷ [N]
= [RESULT] cm

Objects in water appear shallower than they really are. This is why a swimming pool looks less deep than it actually is and why a stick appears bent when placed in water.
